task: Write one sentence of your own using the word artisan. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know artisan should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Every railing scroll on the footbridge carries the initials of the artisan who forged it a century ago.
A hobbyist is milder than an artisan on this scale — making things for the joy of it, with no standard to answer to; the artisan answers for every piece, because the craft is the trade.
A master goes further than an artisan — the artisan commands the craft; the master sets its standards and signs off on everyone else's.

Craftsman is the plain, everyday word for a skilled maker, and most artisans would answer to it. Artisan adds a whiff of tradition and identity: not just someone good with tools, but someone whose handcraft answers to a standard and is owned start to finish — work an artisan would sign.

Artificer is the antique word for the same skilled maker — met in old books and regimental titles, rarely on a shop door. Artisan is its living descendant, the current term for a hand-worker who owns a craft. Reach for artificer only when the prose itself is wearing costume.

In a one-room shop behind her house, Marta Silva makes violin bows the way her teacher's teacher made them, from rough plank to finished silver winding.
She is, by every measure, an artisan: the bow is her trade, her training runs back generations, and every stick that leaves the bench carries her brand.
Factories can turn out a playable bow in an afternoon.
Silva spends three weeks on one.
The difference is not only patience.
When a bow warps years later, players ship it back to her, because her name on the frog means she answers for it.
Ask what she would do if the work stopped selling, and she shrugs: there is no other plan.
